comment: Source read at commit 82b5d6f, the HEAD of https://github.com/regular-dev/hardseqs; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.0.0 manifest and there is no tag for the release. THE SIXTEEN PER-STEP OUTPUTS ARE ONE SAMPLE WIDE. clearAllStepOutputs() at HardSeqs.cpp:151 zeroes all sixteen on every process call, before the clock block at line 162 raises the one for the current step, so each is a single-sample 10V spike rather than a gate; the GATE output at line 178 is not cleared that way and instead follows the clock's high time. The three MOD outputs are cleared by nothing at all, so they hold the last fired step's value until the next clock edge. PARAM_IS_RUN and PARAM_SEL, indices 1 and 3 of the enum, are counted in the call to config() but never given a configParam or a widget, so they have no name, no tooltip and no position and cannot be clicked. The instrument label is parameter 31: HardSeqsWidget.cpp:84 sets it to the new frame number minus one, so the stored value trails the picture by one and a reloaded patch shows the previous name; nothing in process() reads it. The five EACH switches default to 0 in configParam (line 63) while StepEntry starts with all five true (HardSeqs.hpp:135), and setSelectedStep is not called from the constructor, so a newly added module shows them off while the steps behave as though they were on; clicking any step button brings the display into line. The random gate menu items change m_steps directly and do not refresh the GATE switch, so that switch can read stale until a step button is clicked. The bottom-row controls are attached with addChild rather than addParam, which keeps them out of ModuleWidget's parameter list but still leaves them clickable, and the census finds their positions. MOD1 has snapping turned off explicitly (HardSeqsWidget.cpp:178) while MOD2, MOD3, PROB and ELEN are snapping knobs. The probability draw uses std::mt19937 seeded from std::random_device, a fresh draw on each visit to the step. The README at the repository is short and describes POS as 0V for the first step and 5V for the sixteenth, which matches the code.
